A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 56-page versions of the same HSSBench work. Text and rendered-page comparison cover the main paper and Appendices A–D, including image-based case studies, without material comparison gaps.

before.justification: v2 reports original HSSBench model evaluations, human-expert accuracy, dataset analyses, and intervention experiments in Section 3 and Appendices B–D.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including Table 1 and the multilingual, confounding-option, visual-information, and RAG experiments in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The expert/multi-agent VQA generation pipeline is unchanged. Section 2 and Figure 3 retain the same preparation, construction, and validation stages, agent roles, and revision procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same six HSS categories, 45 subtypes, six languages, and multiple-choice/open-ended tasks. The additional Art-category benchmark evaluations in Appendix C.5 are also unchanged.

E2.justification: The evaluated MLLMs, human/random baselines, and comparator membership in the appendix experiments are identical. The newly cited works in Section 4 are not introduced as evaluated comparison methods.

E3.justification: Section 3.1 and Appendix C retain the same prompting strategies, question formats, evaluation procedures, and sample sizes, including the 900-item multilingual/confounding-option samples and 2,000-item evaluator-validation sample.

E4.justification: The human-versus-agent data analysis, confounding-option experiment, image-description interventions, RAG analysis, and Appendix D case studies are retained unchanged. No analysis is added, removed, or revised.

E5.justification: Table 3 retains the same expert-score breakdown, and Appendix C.9 retains the same Fleiss' and Cohen's kappa agreement reporting. There are no changes to repeated-run, seed, uncertainty-interval, or significance-test reporting.

E6.justification: All result tables, plots, and appendix cases are identical. For example, Table 1 retains GPT-4.1's 39.97% overall CoT open-ended accuracy and Qwen2.5-VL-72B-Instruct's 51.87% overall CoT multiple-choice accuracy under the same settings.

T1.justification: Neither version presents a formal theoretical development with propositions or proofs. The benchmark specifications, validation criteria, and evaluation definitions are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion are unchanged. Both claim a multilingual HSS benchmark, an expert/multi-agent construction pipeline, and evidence that HSS tasks challenge current MLLMs.

C2.justification: Both retain the same interpretations concerning CoT hallucinations, weak visual–conceptual integration, cultural influences, distractor vulnerability, and limitations of general-purpose RAG. The qualifications in Appendix A.2 are also unchanged.

D1.justification: The generation-model disclosure, annotation platform, expert profiles, inference/evaluation prompt templates, and stated public repository access are unchanged in Section 2.4, Appendix A, and Tables 17–18.

R1.justification: Section 4 adds three Shuaibo Li et al. references: Image manipulation localization using attentional cross-domain CNN features (2021), Unionformer (2024), and Toward medical deepfake detection (2025). They extend an existing citation list without substantive discussion or changes to HSSBench's research positioning.

P1.justification: Edits are limited to the expanded citation list, corresponding author-year suffix adjustments, new bibliography entries, and the arXiv version/date stamp. The prose, headings, section order, and narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added references cause limited line reflow in Section 4 and bibliography reflow across pages 12–17. All figures, tables, and appendix case-study displays retain identical content and layout.

improvement.justification: v4 expands the references without developing a new comparison or explaining the added works' relationship to HSSBench. The method, empirical evidence, interpretations, appendices, and reproducibility information are unchanged, so the bibliographic and formatting edits do not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
